chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: Our companions may be gathered together in one place, and some of them stand and pray al-ẓuhr while some of them pray al-ʿaṣr. He said: “All of that is broad in allowance.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: our companions; members of the Shia community referred to in the report
key_terms.الْمَكَانِ: the place or shared location where the people are gathered
key_terms.وَاسِعٌ: broad in allowance; indicating permissibility and latitude

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for some people in a gathering to pray al-ẓuhr while others pray al-ʿaṣr?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates flexibility regarding some companions praying al-ẓuhr while others pray al-ʿaṣr when gathered in the same place. It conveys juridical breadth and permissibility in this matter within the framework of salat (prayer).
